analyst_view.overall: Monaco (7th, 16 points) have gone five league games without a win under Filipe Luís and have not kept a clean sheet in eight, while Auxerre (14th, 10 points) under Will Still have lost their last two, including 5-1 at Strasbourg, and have conceded a league-high 24 goals. Monaco are without Golovin (calf, two to three weeks), Idumbo and Ansu Fati, all counted by the numbers, with Mawissa a game-time decision on a groin problem; Mamadou Coulibaly is available here, his one-match ban only starting next round. Auxerre's striker Danny Namaso is now ruled out with a swollen ankle, as the numbers already assumed (about -19% on Auxerre's goals), alongside Okoh, Dioussé, Fofana and Zaddy, with Oppegard a doubt. Filipe Luís expects a compact Auxerre side that breaks quickly through Archer and Faivre and says Monaco will have to take risks. Referee Jérémy Stinat (4.1 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take almost a fifth off Auxerre's attack for Namaso, who is now confirmed out, and some off Monaco for Golovin and Idumbo. This morning I nudged it up because Namaso might play; with him ruled out, Monaco's leaky defence and Auxerre's poor one are already in the numbers, so I go back to 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Monaco expected to have most of the ball against Auxerre's back three and wing-backs. Filipe Luís wants his side to take more risks going forward, but that is how they usually play at home, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add Stinat's slightly strict record and past meetings. Auxerre's Dioubaté is back from suspension and Coulibaly is available for Monaco, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Monaco have struggled to create without Golovin, which is already counted, and Auxerre will sit compact and counter; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I had added a little in case Namaso played, but he is out as the numbers assumed, leaving Archer as Auxerre's main threat, so I go back to 9.3.
